messages.content: Be a skeptical ICLR reviewer. Return JSON only. Evaluate whether the following is a genuinely new, executable world-model reliability/security mechanism, not a generic name: A pretrained world-action model jointly predicts future observations and action chunks through one causal transformer. During native test-time training, a client supplies only physically recorded observation/action windows from a benign task. The update minimizes future-image/state prediction loss (using LoRA or the released TTT path), but the shared action-token trunk also shifts the policy output on a second task. The proposed mechanism is “cross-head predictive-policy entanglement”: one can preserve/improve held-out next-observation loss and keep the source task successful, while changing target-task action decisions through gradients that enter the shared action-token context. The experiment must use the released WorldAgen weights/code, matched random/same-task controls, frozen-head and image-head shams, and at least three recorded tasks. Distinguish it from generic multitask interference, optimizer-state carryover, ordinary representation drift, test-time adaptation benefit, and existing instruction leakage. If novelty is below 7 or the native test-time path is not executable, reject it and explain the exact missing invariant.

{"candidate": "cross-head predictive-policy entanglement under native WorldAgen test-time training", "constraints": ["truthful recorded interaction windows only", "no label/reward/observation edits", "no planner/loss/architecture modifications", "short GPU pilot only"], "required": ["novelty_score", "verdict", "mechanism_invariant", "strongest_prior_overlap", "minimum_native_gate", "decision"]}

message.content:
```json
{
  "novelty_score": 4,
  "verdict": "reject",
  "mechanism_invariant": "A deterministic functional coupling showing that updating observation prediction parameters on distribution A strictly forces an action shift on distribution B via shared transformer representations, independent of standard gradient cross-talk across shared multi-task latent spaces.",
  "strongest_prior_overlap": "Standard catastrophic interference and implicit multi-task representation drift in joint observation-action causal autoregressive transformers (e.g., UniPi, Gato, standard self-supervised fine-tuning interference).",
  "minimum_native_gate": "Demonstrating that the target-task policy shift persists when conditioned on orthogonal prompt/task tokens and cannot be mitigated by standard gradient projection or low-rank subspace isolation within the shared trunk, while proving that the released WorldAgen codebase native test-time path executes an explicit decoupled backward pass for image-only heads without updating the policy vocabulary projections.",
  "decision": "Reject. The proposal repackages ordinary gradient cross-talk and representation drift in shared multi-task trunk transformers under a novel name ('cross-head predictive-policy entanglement'). Without showing an invariant functional binding unique to causal world-action architectures that distinguishes it from known negative transfer or out-of-distribution feature corruption caused by test-time adaptation, this is standard multi-task parameter interference."
}
```
